lines.text: Hi! I am Swiftee.
Remember we learned about polygons before.
Polygons are closed shapes made from straight lines.
Which of these are polygons?
Not quite. A circle is curved. A polygon has only straight sides.
Not quite. This shape is open. A polygon must be closed.
Let’s play with this one.
Select any vertex.
Let’s connect it to another vertex.
This is a side of the polygon.
Let’s connect it to a different vertex.
Yay! You made a diagonal!
A line segment joining two non-adjacent vertices is a diagonal.
Let’s draw another diagonal from the same vertex.
Drop it on a corner!
A diagonal connects non-adjacent vertices.
Your turn! Let’s draw all the diagonals from this vertex.
Drop it on a corner!
A diagonal connects non-adjacent vertices.
Let’s look at the diagonals of this pentagon.
Are the diagonals inside or outside?
The diagonals are inside.
Let’s make a change.
Help me pull this vertex inside.
Pull it in more!
Whoa! One of the diagonals went outside.
Whoa! Some of the diagonals went outside.
Let’s compare the diagonals in both the pentagons.
This one has all the diagonals inside.
But this one has atleast one diagonal outside.
All diagonals inside means convex polygon.
Atleast one diagonal outside means concave polygon.
Drag any vertex to make this polygon concave.
The diagonals are still inside the shape, so it is still convex.
Let me show you. Watch this corner.
Now one diagonal goes outside, so the polygon is concave.
Great job!
Can you sort these polygons as convex or concave?
Yes! It’s convex: no corner goes inward.
Yes! It’s concave: one corner goes inward.
Look! This corner goes inward.
Atleast one diagonal outside means concave polygon.
Look! No corner goes inward.
All diagonals inside means convex polygon.
Hmm… The sides look suspiciously alike.
Let’s measure the sides.
Every side is equal. But what about the angles?
Let’s measure the angles.
The angles match too!
Help me stretch this corner. Let’s see what happens to the sides and angles.
Drag the highlighted vertex.
Try again! Stretch the corner a little further.
It’s still a pentagon. But are the sides and angles still equal?
Try again! Compare the sides and angles now.
The sides and angles changed, so they are not equal.
Let’s compare these two pentagons.
All the sides and angles are equal in this pentagon.
But this pentagon has unequal sides and unequal angles.
All sides and angles equal means a regular polygon. Sides and angles unequal means an irregular polygon.
Where does this polygon belong?
Try again! Every side and every angle is equal.
This one is regular. Every side is equal, and every angle is equal too.
Try again! The sides are not all equal.
This one is irregular. Its sides are not all the same length.
Try again! The angles are not all equal.
This one is irregular. Its sides match, but its angles are not all equal.
Try again! The sides and the angles are not all equal.
This one is irregular. Its sides are not equal, and its angles are not equal either.
